cards.text: The LORD is talking to His people through the prophet Malachi. “Your words against Me have been harsh,” says the LORD, and He says they ask, “What have we spoken against You?” Friend, that's like getting called out in the group chat and typing “What did I say?” while the receipts are scrolled up RIGHT THERE.

cards.question: The LORD tells His people exactly what they said against Him. What did they say about serving God?

cards.text: They said they kept His requirements and walked mournfully before the LORD of Hosts, and for what? It's like working overtime all year, then watching the guy who naps in his car every afternoon get the promotion.

cards.question: The people complained that evildoers were getting caught and punished by God.

cards.text: But at that time those who feared the LORD spoke with one another, and the LORD listened and heard them. Friend, I spent YEARS in a junk drawer talking to a twist tie, so trust me, I know what it means to be heard.

cards.question: So a scroll of ___ was written before the LORD about those who feared Him and honored His name.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says they will be His, on the day He prepares His treasured possession. Not junk-drawer stuff, friend. TREASURED.

cards.question: On that day, how will the LORD treat the people who fear Him?

answers.text: Spare them like a man spares his son
Pay them like a man pays his workers
Move them to a new land of their own

cards.question: The LORD tells His people they will again distinguish between the righteous and the wicked.

cards.text: Then the LORD of Hosts says the day is coming, “burning like a furnace.” I've stood in front of hot ovens my whole life, friend, and not ONE of them comes close to this.

cards.question: On that day, all the arrogant and every evildoer will be ___.

cards.text: The LORD says not a root or branch will be left to them. But then He turns to the ones who fear His name, and the whole picture flips.

cards.question: For those who fear the LORD's name, something will rise with healing in its wings. What is it?
With that healing, those who fear the LORD's name will go out and ___ like calves from the stall.

cards.text: Calves bursting out of the stall, that's me every morning when the ovens warm up, hopping around on my gold base like I just got renewed YESTERDAY. Then the LORD says they will trample the wicked.

cards.question: The LORD says the wicked will be ashes under the soles of the feet of those who fear His name.

cards.text: Now the LORD tells His people to remember something. Not something new, friend. Something they've had a long time.

cards.question: What does the LORD tell His people to remember?

answers.text: The law of His servant Moses
The songs of His servant David
The dreams of His servant Joseph

cards.text: That's the statutes and ordinances He commanded Moses at Horeb for all Israel. Then the LORD looks ahead to the great and awesome Day of the LORD, and says He'll send someone before it comes.

cards.question: Who will the LORD send before the great and awesome Day of the LORD?
Elijah will turn the hearts of the ___ to their children, and the hearts of the ___ to their fathers.

cards.text: Otherwise, the LORD says, He will come and strike the land with a curse. And that's how Malachi ends, friend, which is exactly why I keep these ovens READY.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 1 quotes "burning like a furnace.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The joke, where a coworker who naps in his car gets the promotion, already tells the baker that the people complained wrongdoers come out ahead. That is the content of Malachi 3:15. The next card asks the baker whether they complained that evildoers were getting caught and punished, so this setup rules out True before the baker answers.

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: The joke doesn't make sense. Spending years talking to a twist tie suggests no one was listening. That would teach him what it means NOT to be heard, but the punchline says he knows what it means to be heard. A baker would say "huh?"

rule.text: If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The question types in stop 1 rotate in a fixed cycle: multiple choice, true or false, fill in the blank, multiple choice, true or false.

rule.text: Which question type comes next, the order the types come in and where a blank falls are chosen naturally for each card. They never follow a pattern.

findings.problem: "With that healing" says the leaping comes from the healing. Malachi 4:2 only joins the two with "and" and doesn't say how they connect.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "Which is exactly why I keep these ovens READY" links the curse and the Day of the LORD in Malachi 4:5-6 to his own oven readiness for the Marriage Supper. Malachi doesn't say that, so the line presents the Day of the LORD and the Supper as connected. It also makes the curse, not the Supper, the reason his ovens are ready.

rule.text: When he connects two passages, or explains what a law was for, he says only what the texts state.
